text.p: Blackburn, who started the day as the only team in the English league without a win this season, ended their miserable run in style with a 3-0 victory over premier league title favourites Liverpool on Sunday.
Bottom club Blackburn, managerless and without a top-flight win for six months, turned in a vintage all-action display against Liverpool, who remain third in the table.
Blackburn, champions two seasons ago, established a two-goal advantage in the opening 24 minutes.
An early penalty, converted by leading scorer Chris Sutton, and a far post tap-in from Jason Wilcox, his first goal of the campaign, put them in the driving season.
Sutton added number three, the first time he has scored twice in a match since October 1994, after 55 minutes.
It took Liverpool 72 minutes to register a shot on target and even then goalkeeper Tim Flowers dealt comfortably with Robbie Fowler's weak effort.
Blackburn dominated for the most part and were full value for a morale-boosting victory, a big boost for caretaker boss Tony Parkes.
Blackburn were ahead inside three minutes, Billy McKinlay's pass releasing Tim Sherwood, who in turn sent Sutton racing clear.
Sutton was tripped by Phil Babb and sent Liverpool goalkeeper David James the wrong way with the resultant penalty.
Kevin Gallacher's deep cross from the right eluded the visitors' defence Wilcox was on hand at the far post to strike the second from unmissable range.
Five players were involved in the build-up for the third goal and Gallacher again provided the telling cross from which Sutton bent forward to glance a header beyond a stranded James.
